text:
Nina M.: Quick post-launch thread — 0.8.0 went out this morning. We're seeing a mix of bugs and feature asks from early adopters. Need to decide hotpatch vs 0.8.1 vs backlog. Short: one customer-facing regression, two medium bugs, four enhancement requests.
Carlos V.: Link to tracker with repro + affected customers: https://redwood.atlassian.example/PM-3301
Jae K.: What is the customer-facing regression?
Nina M.: Regression: routing policy sometimes sends requests to a cold model variant, causing ~700ms extra p99 for some routes. Visible in customer telemetry for 2 enterprise orgs.
Carlos V.: That's UX/high-cost impact. Cold routing increases token cost and latency. I'd push for a targeted patch to avoid regressions in SLAs.
Jae K.: Two medium bugs are: 1) dashboard quota table misaggregates on paginated queries, 2) batching estimator sometimes undercounts tokens for long prompts. Both affect observability and billing accuracy. Lower urgency but important for trust.
Nina M.: Enhancements: customer asks for per-route quantization presets, prompt-template UI, improved QA harness for regen tests, and more detailed cost breakdown. Those can backlog unless customers pay for expedited slot.
OpsBot: Next deploy window available: today 20:00 UTC. Hotpatch branch suggested: refs/heads/patch/0.8.0. Runbook: https://confluence.example/runbooks/0.8.x
Carlos V.: Proposal: hotpatch the routing cold-start regression (hotfix) in today's window with a conservative sticky-routing fallback. Move batching estimator + quota aggregation to 0.8.1. Enhancements -> backlog unless a customer escalates.
Jae K.: I can implement a sticky-routing guard quickly: on route selection, prefer warm nodes for the same customer for X minutes. I'll also add a perf regression test. ETA: 3 hours for PR.
Nina M.: Acceptance criteria for hotfix: p99 latency for affected routes reduced to within 10% of pre-release baseline in canary (5% traffic) for 1h and no increase in error rate. If not met, rollback.
Carlos V.: Owners: @Jae K. -> sticky-routing + tests; @Carlos V. -> canary monitor + cost impact analysis; @Nina M. -> customer comms and roadmap update.
Jae K.: Branch steps:
```
git checkout -b patch/0.8.0-sticky-route
# implement guard
git push origin patch/0.8.0-sticky-route
```
Jae K.: Will request reviews and tag SRE for canary alarms.
Nina M.: Locking scope: hotfix = sticky-routing patch + status update. 0.8.1 = batching estimator + quota fix + tests. Backlog = UI & advanced UX requests. Update roadmap row and ETA 0.8.1 for next sprint.
Carlos V.: If any blocker shows up during canary, we escalate to on-call and decide rollback vs iterate.
OpsBot: Canary plan created: https://deploys.redwood.example/DEP-3301 (contains rollback steps)
